note.question: How can shoppertainment live streaming be represented?
note.overview: “Shoppertainment” live streaming, a blend of entertainment and product selling, is becoming increasingly popular. In shoppertainment sessions, streamers face bandwidth constraints so balance between providing product information and entertainment (such as singing, dancing, and storytelling). We conceptualize a shoppertainment live streamer as a novel type of online retail platform that maximizes total commissions from selling a range of manufacturer products.

source.section: A Model of Shoppertainment Live Streaming
source.quote: We conceptualize a shoppertainment live streamer as a novel type of online retail platform that maximizes total commissions from selling a range of manufacturer products.
We assume a manufacturer obtains profit δ ≥0 from the outside option and will contract to sell through the streamer only if anticipating a payoff no lower than δ.
Upon attend­ ing a session, a consumer observes the product’s quality q and price p, receives any additional product informa­ tion provided by the streamer, and decides whether to buy or not.

This notion is best illustrated by Dong Yuhui, the star shop­ pertainment live streamer, who is known for teaching English and sharing life stories during the entire ses­ sion of selling fruits, canned vegetables, and instant noodles, without discussing product features or pushing for purchases.

Consumers do not know which product is being offered or the product price before attending a session and decide whether to attend a ses­ sion based on expected utility from live entertainment and live shopping.
The streamer provides basic information about the product to sell, including product quality q and price p.

Our study investigates how streamers can leverage entertainment bandwidth as a long-term strategy to influence manufacturers’ pricing decisions and consumers’ attendance, as well as purchasing behaviors.

conditions: The streamer collects a commission from each product’s sales revenue, with commission rate α(0 < α < 1) being exogenously determined and common knowledge.
Following Lal and Sarvary (1999) and Zhang et al. (2015), we specify a product’s quality q(0 ≤q ≤1) as the probability that the product fits a consumer’s tastes or personal needs.

Among all manufacturers contracted to sell through the streamer, the product qualities follow a uniform distribution on interval [q,1], where q(0 ≤q ≤1) represents the quality threshold sets by the streamer and is common knowledge.
